text:
Maya Li: Heads-up 1: were launching a preview for 'telemetry-pii-mask' on Private (VPC/on-prem) privacy-mode — opt-in feature to remove or pseudonymize sensitive fields from telemetry before it leaves a customers control plane.
Maya Li: Why: customers with strict privacy/regulatory constraints asked for stronger guarantees that logs/metrics exported for support or analytics won't contain customer PII or secrets. This is focused on the control-plane-side telemetry we collect/export.
Maya Li: What it does (modes):
- redaction: strip matching fields and replace with <REDACTED>
- pseudonymize: reversible mapping stored in local keystore (customer-controlled)
- hash-only: one-way SHA256 of values (useful for correlation without raw data)
Ivan Petrov: Quick note on performance: masking happens asynchronously before export. Expect a small CPU/latency delta for very high-volume customers (~1-3% CPU). We'll ship perf graphs in the preview package.
Maya Li: Rollout: canary in pk-staging-7 tomorrow 10:30 PT, limited preview invites in 10 days, broader preview in 4 weeks. GA TBD after compliance sign-off.
Maya Li: How to enable (example config snippet for private-control-plane.yaml):
```
telemetry: 
  pii_masking: 
    enabled: true
    mode: pseudonymize
    patterns:
      - path: "request.user.email"
        type: email
      - path: "request.user.ip"
        type: ip
    export_targets:
      - s3://redwood-telemetry-exports/customer-t-99
```
Maya Li: Important: by default the pseudonymization key is stored in the local KMS. For Private air-gapped installs customers can bring their own key material or use our offline key-wrap flow.
Aisha Khan: Legal: we validated the feature with Compliance. Customers must sign the "Telemetry Masking Data Addendum" if they want Redwood to operate the export pipeline. If they self-host exports completely inside VPC, addendum not required.
Maya Li: Support workflow: if Support needs full plaintext logs for emergency root cause, there's a gated "temporary-unmask" path requiring customer approval + two Redwood approvers. All unmask events are logged and an audit bundle is produced.
Ivan Petrov: For on-prem agents: agent-side masking is also supported in 2.5.1 agent build. If you enable masking at control-plane *and* agent, we short-circuit export to ensure no unmasked copy leaves the tenant perimeter.
Maya Li: CLI to preview masked export (demo):
```
redwoodctl private export-telemetry --tenant t-099 --masking-mode pseudonymize --preview > export-preview.json
jq .exported_items_count export-preview.json
```
Maya Li: Edge cases: nested JSON with base64-encoded blobs may require custom patterns. We're shipping a pattern-testing tool in the preview CLI. Please try it with customer samples (anonymized) and file bugs.
Aisha Khan: Ops checklist: include the masking key rotation step in on-call runbooks. Key rotation invalidates reversible pseudonyms unless key-wrap enabled; doc will be explicit about that.
Maya Li: UI: preview Console tile will show current masking mode + sample masked fields (sanitized) and export targets. Customers requested an "opt-out for support exports" switch we declined it for preview — we want strict defaults.
Legal: Note for sales: dont promise masking guarantees before customers sign the addendum. Also flag any customers in EU who may need additional DPAs.

Maya Li: Thank you. Please post issues with label private-telemetry-mask-preview and drop any customer samples into the secure ticket.
